subject: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Private deployment onboarding
messages:
From: Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@pentahealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@pentahealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Redwood Private onboarding

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our vendor intake for the Private deployment (PHI in-scope), our InfoSec team asked for a detailed vendor roster and a data-path crosswalk for any third parties that touch customer data during inference and telemetry pipelines. Specifically we need:

- A current subprocessor/vendor roster (name, country of processing, role: processing/storage/telemetry)
- Which vendors see unredacted request/response content vs. hashed/aggregated telemetry
- Where encryption keys are managed (Redwood KMS / customer-managed / HSM vendor)
- Data retention defaults and whether logs containing customer prompt text are retained anywhere outside the EU/US region
- Any outbound transfer paths (e.g., analytics relays, cloud marketplaces, crash-reporting)

Attached is our standard security questionnaire (pdf). Can you provide the roster + crosswalk spreadsheet ahead of our risk review next Thursday (23 May)? If there are any vendors that access live PHI, call that out explicitly.

Appreciate it —
Samantha
Samantha Ho
Head of Security Operations, PentaHealth

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@pentahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Redwood Private onboarding

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the note and the questionnaire. We can absolutely provide a single-crosswalk view that maps each third party to the processing role, country, and whether they see cleartext request/response payloads. A couple of clarifying points before we deliver:

- When you say "PHI in-scope", do you require that telemetry (sampling, traces, metrics) is treated as PHI when it could contain user prompt text? We often separate telemetry (aggregated metrics) from request/response logs, but for strict PHI customers we can show a stricter retention policy and options to disable request logging.
- Do you need the full contract-level subprocessor agreement wording, or will a manifest + per-vendor evidence (SOC2 links, encryption attestation) be sufficient for the risk team?

Plan: I will attach a CSV manifest with current processors and a draft crosswalk workbook by EOD Tue (21 May). Marissa (legal) and Ben (security) are looped in for any contractual / technical clarifications. If you'd prefer, we can do a 30-min sync on Wed to walk the matrix.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_manifest_20290519.csv (stub)

From: PentaHealth Security <security@pentahealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: samantha.ho@pentahealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Redwood Private onboarding

Karthik —

Thanks. A couple of answers and asks from InfoSec:

- Telemetry: If request/response logging could include patient identifiers or PHI, we will consider telemetry in-scope. Please mark any processor that touches raw request/response as "PHI-accessor".
- KMS: we require clear mapping for any customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed keys. If Redwood offers an HSM-backed KMS, include vendor and region.
- For now a manifest + hashes of contracts / SOC2 reports is fine for triage; for final approval we'll need the signed DPA + subprocessor appendix.

Also: can you confirm whether any telemetry is routed through third-party analytics (e.g., Mixpanel/Amplitude) during Private deploy setups or if that's only used in Hosted?

Regards,
Marcus Lee
Technical Lead, InfoSec — PentaHealth

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lee <security@pentahealth.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: samantha.ho@pentahealth.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Redwood Private onboarding

Marcus / Samantha —

Quick legal note to accelerate review: we can provide the full subprocessor roster and a crosswalk workbook that flags PHI-accessor vendors and KMS boundaries. For customers requiring additional contractual granularity, our standard process is:

1) Provide an anonymized manifest + evidence links for triage (SOC2, encryption attestations).
2) Execute the DPA + subprocessor appendix (DocuSign).
3) Once DPA is executed, we provide the redacted-to-full roster (names, contact points) and any requested onshore routing attestations.

If PentaHealth needs the full roster pre-DPA, we are open to an NDA and scoped data exposure agreement; otherwise step 1 is typically sufficient for risk triage. I'll prepare the draft DPA addendum language (limited to PHI-accessor handling) and attach a DocuSign envelope you can route to procurement legal.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@pentahealth.com>, Marcus Lee <security@pentahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + data-path crosswalk for Redwood Private onboarding

Team —

Following up after Marissa's note: attached is the crosswalk workbook (redwood-penta-crosswalk-20290522.xlsx). Highlights:

- PHI-accessor vendors: three entries (EdgeEncryptor Inc. — key escrow/HSM, TelemetryRelay Ltd. — optional aggregated metrics only, OnPremLogStore LLC — on-prem customer log retention option).
- KMS: by default Redwood-managed KMS (HSM-backed, vendor: SecureKeyCorp, region: us-west-2). We have a customer-managed-key option (bring-your-own-kms) for Private deployments; details in the workbook.
- Telemetry: default Private deployments do not route live request/response content to third-party analytics. TelemetryRelay Ltd is used for aggregated metrics in Hosted only; listed as "No" under "sees_cleartext_requests" for Private.
- Retention: request logs are off by default for PHI-enabled Private deployments. If enabled by admin, logs are retained for a configurable 30/90/365 day window; retention settings are called out per-tenant in the workbook.

Next steps: 1) Marissa will send a DocuSign DPA addendum for PHI-accessor handling; 2) If you approve the workbook for triage, we can schedule the Wed 23 May risk review.

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-penta-crosswalk-20290522.xlsx (stub)
